subject: Priority capacity standup for pipeline commits
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Huang <sara@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priority capacity standup: Acme dedicated commit pipeline

Team,

Acme is moving to a formal PO for a Dedicated capacity commit — preliminary ask is ~50k GPU hours across p4d/p3 equivalents, starting in July and running ~3 months. Finance flagged that they want a reserved slot mapping and an estimate for burst availability before we approve credits.

Asks:
- Infra (Laura/Marcus): can you confirm if we can carve out a 10-node reserved pool in July and where we would source burst capacity if usage spikes?
- Finance (Kim): an initial draft of pricing/discount tiers for a 3-mo commit (we discussed ~10% at last deal review) so we can include with the PO.
- Sales (Ben/Jordan): I’ll coordinate timing with Acme; they want an answer by end of week.

I know this is tight — requesting a quick standup thread so we can lock whether this becomes a Dedicated reserve or a hybrid (reserved + burst).

Attached: Acme_MVP_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks,
Jordan
--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority capacity standup: Acme dedicated commit pipeline

Jordan — quick update from infra side after a fast check with pool schedulers: 

Summary:
- We can provision a 10-node reserved pool by the first week of July by reallocating 6 nodes from Q3 flexible slots + 4 cold nodes from the lab pool. That gives ~12k guaranteed GPU hours/month (p4d-equivalent) if we maintain 24/7 allocation.
- Burst plan: we have ~6 nodes available in the on-demand burst pool for short windows (48-72 hour spikes). If Acme needs sustained >10% spike above reserved, we’ll need additional burst credit agreements or to convert some of the flexible slots to dedicated.

Risks & constraints:
- Cold-node rework requires a 48-hour maintenance window (we can schedule in the July 3–4 window).
- If Acme requires predictable low-latency N-to-N saturation (heavy cross-node communication), we should avoid mixing instance types — recommend all p4d-similar.

Actionables:
- Marcus to confirm exact node IDs and tag them for Acme by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll add a pool mapping doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-capacity-docs (attached: pool_mapping_v3.pdf).

If finance can confirm the discount band, we can hold these nodes for the PO.

Laura
Lead Infrastructure Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority capacity standup: Acme dedicated commit pipeline

Thanks Laura — helpful. Quick notes from finance/pricing perspective: 

Pricing draft:
- Baseline 3-mo reserved commit (50k GPU hours): list price estimate $360k USD (tokenized to hours).
- Proposed commit discount tiers: 5% @ 25k+, 10% @ 45k+, 15% @ 75k+. For ACME I recommend 10% (deal value and logo + pilot history).
- Burst credit pricing: chargeable at 1.8x list for on-demand bursts; recommend we include a capped burst budget (e.g., 6k hours) covered at commit price then bill overage at on-demand.

Operational notes:
- We need an SLA appendix if they expect guaranteed latency (adds to cost).
- Please confirm whether the reserved nodes will be tagged as "isolated/dedicated" (affects scheduling).

Attached: draft_invoice_acme_3mo.xlsx

I’ll prepare a one-page summary for the PO template. If infra can reserve nodes by EOD Fri and sales secures the signed MSA, finance can issue a pro forma invoice for their procurement team.

-Kim
Director, Revenue Operations & Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Huang <sara@acme.ai>, acct-payments@acme.ai
Date: 2026-06-18T12:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority capacity standup: Acme dedicated commit pipeline

Looping back with a short summary and owners — sending to Acme in one note after internal confirmation. (Quoted below is Sara's note acknowledging timeline.)

Subject: Re: Capacity question

Jordan — thanks, we can target a signed PO by Friday but need your commitment on node availability to include in our procurement paperwork.

----- End forwarded message -----

Internal next steps (owners):
- Infra (Marcus/Laura): reserve 10 nodes (IDs to be provided) and mark as "Acme-dedicated-temp" by EOD Friday. Owner: Marcus Lin.
- Finance (Kim): finalize the one-pager + pro forma and hold a draft invoice for Acme procurement. Owner: Kimberly Park.
- Sales (Jordan/Ben): confirm final pricing and secure signed MSA/PO by Friday COB; I’ll send the combined note to Sara once we have node IDs and the pro forma. Owner: Ben Carter.

If anyone sees a blocker (scheduling, SLA, or pricing) call it out now — otherwise I’ll assemble the message to Acme and include the attachments.

Attachments referenced above: Acme_MVP_capacity_request.xlsx, pool_mapping_v3.pdf, draft_invoice_acme_3mo.xlsx

Ben Carter
